name: Waqrapukara
region: Acos, Acomayo province, above the Apurímac canyon
why: A sanctuary of the Canchis, later taken by the Incas, built around a horn-shaped rock tower at about 4,100 m on the edge of the cliffs over the Apurímac canyon.
book: Entry about S/20 for foreigners (cash), paid at the site. By road from Cusco towards Sicuani, over the Chuquicahuana bridge to Acomayo and Acos and up the unpaved road to the trailhead; most people come on a day tour.
water: None on the way: carry 1.5-2 litres.
dangers: Altitude about 4,100 m at the site: only after acclimatizing in Cusco.
Sheer drops around the rock towers, no railings.
Afternoon cloud and hail in the wet months; the dirt road gets muddy.
turnaround: Thunder or hail: leave the exposed ridge at once and walk back to the vehicle.

points.name: Waqrapukara trailhead
points.note: The end of the dirt road from Acos, on the high grassland. The path heads north-east along the rim of the canyon.

points.name: Waqrapukara fortress
points.note: The two rock horns that give the place its name ('horn fortress'), with Inca walls, niches and terraces on the cliff edge above the Apurímac. Return the same way.
